State compression (状态压缩): when a state is "which of n ≤ 20 things are used", store the set as the bits of one integer S, 0 … 2n − 1. Bit i is 1 when item i is in the set (基础篇第19章). The DP array is indexed by S directly.
220 ≈ 10⁶ sets is fine, 225 is about the limit. Seeing n ≤ 15 … 20 in a problem about sets, orders or paths is the hint.

text: Travelling salesman: f[S][i] = shortest route that starts at city 0, visits exactly the set S, and stands at i. Only S and i matter for the future, not the order inside S. O(2ⁿ · n²) instead of n!.
Adding a city only makes S larger as a number, so the plain loop S = 0, 1, 2, … is a valid order. Best tour here: 0 → 2 → 3 → 1 → 0 = 9 + 8 + 3 + 1 = 21.
Not every bitmask problem is a DP over subsets: here the masks are nodes of a graph and switches are edges, so a BFS finds the fewest presses (P2622). 2ⁿ nodes × m edges.
Read the rule carefully: "1: turn off if on" is T &= ~(1 << j), whatever the light was; "−1: turn on if off" is T |= 1 << j. Press switch 2 then switch 1: 111 → 101 → 000.
Row-by-row masks; precomputed valid rows; subset enumeration.
row 1: fertile 111 row 2: fertile 010 valid rows: no two neighbours, inside fertile

Row by row (逐行状压): on a grid with up to about 12 columns, the state is the mask of the current row. f[i][S] = number of ways for rows 1..i with row i chosen as S. A row is valid alone if S & (S << 1) == 0 (no two neighbours) and S fits the fertile cells.
Two rows are compatible when S & T == 0 (nothing directly above). Precompute the valid masks of a row once: for 12 columns only 377 of the 4096 masks survive, which makes the double loop fast.

Corn fields (P1879): count the ways to plant so that no two planted squares share an edge. Row 1 may be 000, 001, 010, 100, 101 and row 2 may be 000 or 010; 010 under a row using the middle is not allowed.
Total 9.
Artillery (P2704 炮兵阵地) reaches two rows up, so the state holds the last two rows: f[i][S][T]. Kings (P1896 互不侵犯) also forbid diagonal neighbours and add a count of pieces as a third index.

Kings on an n × n board, exactly K of them, none attacking (P1896). Compatible rows: no overlap straight above (S & T) or diagonally (S & (T << 1), S & (T >> 1)). The extra index k counts kings so far.
Counts reach about 10¹⁸ for n = 9, so long long. The popcount of each valid mask is stored once next to it, instead of recomputing it inside the triple loop.

Enumerating subsets of S: for (int T = S; T > 0; T = (T - 1) & S) visits every non-empty subset T of S in decreasing order. Doing this for every S costs 3ⁿ in total (each item is in T, in S only, or outside). Used when a set is split into two groups, as in 宝藏(P3959) and 愤怒的小鸟(P2831).

title: 状态压缩与其他算法的交叉应用

text: Inclusion-exclusion, counting cycles, expectations.

Bitmasks also mix with other techniques: inclusion-exclusion over a small set of conditions (each subset of "violated" conditions is a mask), counting cycles in a small graph, and expected values where the state remembers what has been collected.

Coin shopping (P1450): 4 coin types, each with a limit, 1000 queries. Count with no limits once (unbounded knapsack). Then subtract the ways that break a limit: paying (di + 1) coins of type i up front forces a violation. Inclusion-exclusion over the 16 masks of violated types.
Sign = (−1)popcount(S). Each query costs 16 operations after one shared DP; a bounded knapsack per query would be far too slow.

Counting simple cycles (CF11D): f[S][v] = paths that start at the smallest vertex of S, visit exactly S, and end at v. Fixing the start as the lowest bit stops counting the same cycle from every vertex; dividing by 2 removes the two directions.
In K4 there are 4 triangles and 3 four-cycles: 7. Only extend to vertices larger than the start (u > start), and close the cycle only with ≥ 3 vertices.

Expected values with masks: in 奖励关(P2473) each treasure needs a set of earlier treasures, so the state is (round, mask collected) and the DP runs backwards from the last round, taking the better of "take it" and "skip it". Bill's challenge (P2167) counts strings matching exactly k patterns with f[position][mask of patterns still matching].
Memory is 2ⁿ × (other indices): f[1 << 19][19] long long is 80 MB. Drop a dimension when you can (keep only the last row of a row-by-row DP) and check the limit before choosing n-dependent sizes.
The Luogu problems for this chapter, a ladder through them, and experiments to try yourself.
Key points to memorise
1. Set of n ≤ 20 items = integer S; bit i set ⇔ item i in S.
2. Test S >> i & 1; add S | 1 << i; remove S & ~(1 << i); full (1 << n) − 1.
3. TSP: f[S][i] = shortest visiting S, standing at i; S increasing is a valid order.
4. Masks can be graph nodes: BFS over states.
5. Row DP: valid row S & (S << 1) == 0; compatible rows S & T == 0; precompute valid masks.
6. Subsets of S: T = (T − 1) & S; over all S: 3ⁿ.
7. Inclusion-exclusion: sign (−1)^popcount(S) over violated conditions.
8. Cycles: start at the lowest bit; divide by 2 for direction.
